entry.title: Historic Rail Car Reunited With Dillard Depot After 16-Year Restoration
entry.summary: After 16 years of restoration, an 1883 rail car that once stopped at the Dillard Depot is open to visitors at the Douglas County Museum. The car now sits beside the restored depot it served more than a century ago.

entry.title: Roseburg Chamber to Host Candidates in Focus Forum Oct. 12
entry.summary: The Roseburg Area Chamber of Commerce will host Candidates in Focus on Oct. 12 at the Douglas County Fairgrounds. Admission is free with registration. The Roseburg Receiver and The Roseburg Plug will provide a live feed for those who cannot attend.

entry.title: UCAN Empty Bowls Dinner to raise food bank funds, highlight local food and craft
entry.summary: As food insecurity rates continue to rise in Douglas County, Roseburg residents get a chance to help fight them next weekend by enjoying food and local craftsmanship at the United Community Action Network's (UCAN) Empty Bowls Dinner.

entry.summary: Roseburg Blocktober Fest returns downtown Oct. 3 with five Community Stage acts, food, vendors, family activities, and the Umpqua Valley Farmers Market. The free festival runs from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.

entry.summary: Roseburg police reported three incidents in their latest patrol log: a warrant arrest, a methamphetamine possession citation, and a DUII arrest involving fentanyl charges.

entry.title: Umpqua National Forest Announces Tentative Fall Campground Closure Schedule
entry.summary: Umpqua National Forest has released its tentative fall campground closure schedule. Some campgrounds are already closed, while others will remain open year-round with winter stays available on a first-come, first-served basis.

entry.title: Roseburg Council to Consider $289,020 Stewart Park Master Plan Contract
entry.summary: Roseburg City Council will consider a $289,020 contract to update the Stewart Park Master Plan, including Gaddis Park and the Umpqua Greenway. The planning work could be finished in fall 2027.

entry.title: Diamond Lake Boulevard Improvement Plan Heads to Roseburg Council Work Study
entry.summary: Roseburg councilors will review a draft Diamond Lake Boulevard and OR 138E corridor plan Monday. It identifies 51 potential transportation projects estimated at $90 million; no adoption vote is scheduled.

entry.title: Roseburg Council to Decide Whether to Keep Exploring Downtown Parking Lots for Urban Campground
entry.summary: Roseburg councilors will decide whether to stop, continue, or advance study of the Phillips and Shalimar parking lots as possible urban campground sites. No campground approval is on Monday’s agenda.

entry.title: Roseburg Council to Consider $1 Million Grant Application for UCC Student Housing Downtown
entry.summary: Roseburg City Council will consider applying for a $1 million Business Oregon grant on UCC’s behalf for student housing at the former downtown post office. Approval would authorize an application, not award funding.

entry.title: Roseburg Police to Discuss Flock License Plate Cameras at Monday Council Meeting
entry.summary: Roseburg police will brief City Council on the city’s 15 Flock license plate reader cameras Monday, including how the data is used, retained, and shared. No vote is scheduled.

entry.title: Some Oregon SNAP and TANF Recipients Must Provide Income Information by Sept. 28
entry.summary: Some Oregon SNAP and TANF recipients have until Sept. 28 to provide updated income information. ODHS says benefits may be reduced or a case may close if it does not receive a response.

entry.title: Roseburg Public Library Announces Fall Programs for Children and Teens
entry.summary: Roseburg Public Library’s free fall youth programs include storytimes, book club, crafts, building activities, teen events, volunteer hours, and chess club. Programs run from October through December, and no library card is required.

entry.title: DFPA Public Fire Restrictions Drop to Low Friday; Industrial Level Drops to 1
entry.summary: DFPA will lower public fire restrictions to low and industrial restrictions to Level 1 at 12:01 a.m. Friday, Sept. 25. Some outdoor equipment use will be allowed all day, but debris burning remains prohibited.

entry.title: 180-Acre Prescribed Burn Planned Near Glide as Early as September 29
entry.summary: A 180-acre prescribed burn at the North Bank Habitat Management Area could begin as early as September 29, weather permitting. Smoke may be visible near Glide, and several roads, trails, and access areas could be affected.

entry.title: Roseburg Woman Cited After Crash on West Harvard Avenue With Infant in Vehicle
entry.summary: A Roseburg woman was cited on suspicion of DUII, reckless driving, and reckless endangering after police said her SUV struck a tree on West Harvard Avenue late Wednesday. Her 4-month-old daughter was in the vehicle and was uninjured.

entry.title: Kotek Orders Oregon to Develop Safety Standards for Advanced AI Used by State Agencies
entry.summary: Gov. Tina Kotek has ordered Oregon to develop safety standards for advanced AI used by state agencies. The state’s chief information officer has 90 days to propose how independent reviews would work and whether a “kill switch” requirement is viable.

entry.title: Rain Expected in Roseburg Tonight, Cooler Weather to Follow
entry.summary: Roseburg could reach 81 degrees Thursday before rain arrives tonight. Friday’s high is expected to be near 64, with a chance of showers and isolated thunderstorms. Cooler, mostly dry weather follows this weekend.
